feature.title: Feature flags
feature.intro: The flag select, the assignments tables and the edit-expiration sentence on A-06 and A-15 draw a feature by its label. What each flag does is read from the backend, not guessed.

values.label: Qwen model
values.what: The flag for the Qwen model; an experiment grants it to its participants (`experiment/experiment.service.ts:609`).

values.label: No usage limit
values.what: Removes the usage limit for the class or user. The flag exempts; it does not set a limit, so "Usage limit" would say the opposite.

values.label: R in the scratchpad
values.what: Shows R beside Python in the scratchpad (`ClassIDE.tsx:134`); a class flag applies to that class, a user flag to every class.

engine.title: Models
engine.intro: The model names table above is the lookup; the rows list both ids at each place that draws one.

values.label: Pending
values.what: Enrolled in a class by email, with no account yet: the pending enrollment (`class/class.service.ts:228`) takes effect when the person first signs in (`webhooks/webhook-event.service.ts:323`).

role.title: Role
role.intro: A person's role as a chip, a line under their email or a role chip on an app screen (`user.role`, an app screen's allowed roles). "Professor" is never drawn (terminology: instructor).

values.label: User
values.what: An account that is neither an instructor nor an admin (the users page's role filter and role select).

values.label: Instructor
values.what: What a class enrollment calls an instructor of that class (`auth.guard.ts:124`); the roster, the recipient lists and the email dialog show it (`ClassEnroll.tsx:389`).

registration-result.title: Account creation result
registration-result.intro: The Status column of the results table under "Create password accounts" (`result.status`). Each row's own message is the Error column.

values.label: Waiting
values.what: Not tried yet; the rows are tried one after another.

delivery-status.title: Webhook delivery status
delivery-status.intro: The Status column of a webhook's delivery history (`delivery.status`).

event-status.title: Webhook event status
event-status.intro: The status chip in an event's details (`event.status`).

values.label: Rejected
values.what: Final: an event that is not pending cannot be approved or rejected again (`webhooks/webhook-event.service.ts:178`).

values.label: Not run
values.what: The approved action did not run.

audit-action.title: Audit action
audit-action.intro: The Action column of the audit history and details (`audit.action`).

placement.title: App screen placement
placement.intro: Where a registered app's screen is shown, in the registry's screens table (`ui.placement`).

category.title: App category
category.intro: A registered app's category chip (`app.category`). The category is the app's own text, so a value not listed is drawn as written.

experiment-status.title: Experiment status
experiment-status.intro: An experiment's status where the student chat's experiment picker lists it (`experiment.status`); the experiments pages already use these labels (`experimentUi.tsx`).

class.title: A class
class.shown: the class's name (`classControllerGetById(...).className`, the read `AdminLayout.tsx:340` already makes)
class.intro: A class id is a UUID. Wherever a page draws one, it draws the class's name instead, in a select, a chip, a table cell or a sentence; a class with no name reads "Untitled class" (SR-1.11), never its id.

user.title: A user
user.shown: the user's email address (the Users page's own column)
user.intro: A user id is a UUID. A table cell or sentence that names a user draws the email address; a user who cannot be read reads "Unknown user", never the id.

activity.title: Webhook state
activity.intro: A webhook's state chip in the webhooks table (`webhook.isActive`).

webhook.title: A webhook
webhook.shown: its address, the URL the admin entered
webhook.intro: A webhook id is a UUID. A subtitle or sentence that names a webhook draws its address; a column or row labelled "Webhook ID" is the one place the id itself is drawn (an admin copies it).

reasons.labelled: labelled as an id ("Webhook ID", "Event ID", "Audit ID", "Session ID", "ID:"): the id is the content, and an admin copies it to find the record
reasons.caption: the caption under a user's email: it keeps a row identifiable when the email is empty
reasons.chosen: an identifier the admin chose or typed (an app's identifier, a scope, a variant key): it is the name the admin knows it by
reasons.event: an event name is the API's identifier: an admin subscribes to it by name in the Events field
reasons.word: a word inside a sentence or beside a number (a count's noun, hour or day, enabled or disabled): the sentence has its own rows
reasons.text: a message or a status sentence, not an identifier
reasons.display: already display text (a permission's name, a chunk's type)
reasons.mapped: already a label: the mapping rows A-03.24 and A-03.25 name the legend entries
reasons.asis: the value as written for an unknown value: an id that is not listed is never hidden
reasons.address: the app's identifier as the page's own address spells it: the person asked for that page by it, and an app that is not enabled has no name to show
reasons.anonymous: a code designed to be read: the analytics numbers a class's students anonymously (s3 for Student 3) and the badge shows the number
reasons.acronym: an acronym drawn in capitals (HTTP, SSE): the guide spells acronyms as they are
reasons.registered: an identifier the app's developer registered and the admin reads (a screen's slug, a prompt's id): the app and the admin know the item by it, and it is the name the app's own documentation uses

batches.why: a read: the loop loads each class's details for the registration form, changes nothing, and leaves out a class it cannot read without a message to word; the failure of the list itself is A-11.30. Whether the form should say that some classes are missing is a Stage 2 question (it needs a place to say it).
